title: Conformance matrix, Phase 4 (SMF: Nsmf_PDUSession, 5GSM, N2 SM information, N4, modification, recovery, paging, persistence)
note: Same rules as the other matrices: every test reference, function and clause is checked by tools/check/check_matrix.py. verified = tests pass and a real peer or a capture confirms it (Open5GS AMF + UERANSIM against our SMF with our UDM, PCF and UPF, scenarios S1-S4 with OUR_SMF=1). The gap rows are what the phase leaves out; they are listed so nothing is hidden.

rows.procedure: Create SM Context: multipart request with the N1 SM part, subscription check, UPF selection, address allocation, UDM registration, SM policy, N4 establishment, 201 with Location
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AMF creates the SM context of a UERANSIM UE against our SMF in oracle scenarios S1-S3 (OUR_SMF=1 with our UDM, PCF and UPF): registration, PDU session, ping through our UPF, release and deregistration pass.

rows.procedure: Create SM Context refusals: bad body, unknown DNN / subscriber / slice, disallowed PDU session type, pool exhausted, no UPF, unsupported request type; the PDU Session Establishment Reject travels as the N1 part of the error body
rows.evidence: Scripted AMF. The reject message and the 5GSM cause are decoded again with the NAS library; no refused request leaves anything behind in the SMF, UPF, PCF, UDM or address pool.

rows.procedure: Update SM Context, user plane activation: PDU_RES_SETUP_RSP from the gNB turns the downlink FAR to the gNB tunnel
rows.evidence: UERANSIM's gNB answers the N2 setup request our SMF built; the ping in S2 runs through the downlink tunnel the SMF configured from its response.

rows.procedure: Update SM Context, user plane deactivation (AN release): downlink buffered in the UPF, the report answered and turned into a page
rows.evidence: Scripted AMF and gNB against the real UPF runtime; the buffered packet is delivered after reactivation.

rows.procedure: Update SM Context, service request (ACTIVATING): the N2 setup request is returned in the response
rows.evidence: Scripted AMF; the returned transfer decodes and carries the UPF's tunnel.

rows.procedure: UE-requested PDU session release: release request answered with the release command and the N2 release command, resources freed on the release complete / N2 release response
rows.evidence: S3 releases the PDU session from the UE (nr-cli ps-release) through Open5GS's AMF; the SMF frees UPF, PCF, UDM and the address.

rows.procedure: Release SM Context (AMF-initiated, e.g. deregistration)
rows.evidence: S3 deregisters the UE with an active session; our SMF releases it. Unknown contexts answer 404.

rows.procedure: A second establishment of the same PDU session id replaces the first (the AMF-requested release of the duplicate)
rows.evidence: Both contexts are accounted for: the old reference is gone, one UPF session, one PCF association, one address in use.

rows.procedure: Multipart/related framing of the SM context bodies (JSON part, N1 and N2 binary parts addressed by Content-Id)
rows.evidence: Parsed and built bodies interoperate with Open5GS's AMF in both directions (create, N1N2 transfer, modify).

rows.procedure: SM context status notification to the AMF when the SMF releases a context on its own (AMF refused the transfer, UPF lost)
rows.evidence: The AMF's status endpoint receives RELEASED with the cause after the release command has been delivered.

rows.procedure: N1N2MessageTransfer with the PDU Session Establishment Accept and the PDU session resource setup request (deferred until the 201 is out)
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AMF accepts the transfer and sends the accept to the UE and the setup request to the gNB; a refusal by the AMF makes the SMF give the session back. The AMF address is taken from the smContextStatusUri (or smf.amf.uri); NRF discovery is later.

rows.procedure: PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT: selected type and SSC mode, QoS rules, Session-AMBR, PDU address, S-NSSAI, DNN, optional cause and PCO
rows.evidence: UERANSIM accepts the message and brings up its tunnel interface with the allocated address.

rows.procedure: Authorized QoS rules (default rule and one rule per PCC rule, packet filter components from the IPFilterRule, precedence 80 avoided)
rows.evidence: Byte-exact expected encodings for the default rule and a two-filter rule, including the match-all restriction for downlink-only filters.

rows.procedure: Authorized QoS flow descriptions for the non-default flows (5QI, GFBR, MFBR)
rows.evidence: Byte-level checks of a GBR and a non-GBR flow description.

rows.procedure: Session-AMBR coding (unit = 4^(n-1) kbit/s, value rounded up to 16 bits)
rows.evidence: Boundary values checked; the UE accepts the 100/200 Mbit/s values in S3.

rows.procedure: PDU address for IPv4, IPv6 (interface identifier) and IPv4v6
rows.evidence: IPv4 is verified end to end. IPv6 and IPv4v6 are encoded, allocated and completed by a router advertisement, tested against our UPF; no IPv6 UE has run against Open5GS's AMF and UERANSIM, and N3 over IPv6 is not supported by the UPF.

rows.procedure: Extended protocol configuration options: DNS server (IPv4/IPv6) and IPv4 link MTU replies to what the UE asked for
rows.evidence: Container identifiers are those of the pinned TS 24.008 v16.7.0.

rows.procedure: PDU session type selection: requested type if subscribed, else the allowed single stack with cause #50 / #51, else reject #28
rows.evidence: Dual stack, narrowing to IPv6 only, and refusal of IPv6 on an IPv4-only subscription.

rows.procedure: PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REJECT with the matching 5GSM cause (#26, #27, #28, #38, #96, #97)
rows.evidence: Decoded again from the multipart error body.

rows.procedure: Malformed or foreign 5GSM input is refused without reading out of bounds (truncations, wrong EPD, wrong PSI, wrong message type)
rows.evidence: Replay fuzzing with mutations under ASan/UBSan.

rows.procedure: PDUSessionResourceSetupRequestTransfer: UL NG-U tunnel, PDU session type, session AMBR, QoS flow list with ARP and GBR information
rows.evidence: UERANSIM's gNB decodes the transfer and answers with its tunnel in S2/S3.

rows.procedure: PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer and ...UnsuccessfulTransfer parsing (IPv4, IPv6, dual-stack addresses; accepted flow list; cause)
rows.evidence: The gNB's response in S2/S3 yields the downlink tunnel used for the ping.

rows.procedure: PDUSessionResourceReleaseCommandTransfer
rows.evidence: Accepted by Open5GS's AMF and the gNB in the UE-requested release of S3.

rows.procedure: PFCP Association Setup initiated by the SMF, heartbeats, association accepted from a configured UPF
rows.evidence: Associates with our UPF in every oracle scenario; Open5GS's UPF-initiated association is accepted from a configured address.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Establishment from the policy: default PDRs, one PDR pair per PCC rule, FARs, session QER and one QER per flow, BAR, PDN Type, DNN, S-NSSAI
rows.evidence: Accepted by our UPF engine and runtime; the first request of each type matches Open5GS's SMF element for element apart from the documented allow-list (pfcp_diff.py --smf).

rows.procedure: PCC rule -> PDR/FAR/QER mapping table, including the SDF filter direction rule (the Flow Description is copied unchanged to uplink and downlink PDRs; the UPF swaps for ACCESS) and per-flow QFI marking
rows.evidence: Table-driven against the real UPF engine: downlink packets matching each rule leave with the QFI of that rule's flow; uplink goes through the tunnel.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Modification: downlink FAR to the gNB tunnel (activate) and to buffering with downlink-data notification (deactivate)
rows.evidence: The ping of S2 depends on it.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Deletion
rows.evidence: Every release path ends with the UPF session gone.

rows.procedure: PFCP Session Report Request (downlink data) answered with the right SEID and cause; unknown sessions answered with Session Not Found
rows.evidence: The Session Report Response is counted by the UPF.

rows.procedure: Request retransmission (T1/N1), loss of a UPF detected by heartbeats, restart detected by the Recovery Time Stamp
rows.evidence: UPF stopped and restarted on the same ports: no UPF is selected while it is down, the restart is counted, its sessions are released, new sessions work again.

rows.procedure: Differential PFCP analysis of the SMF: same UPF and scenario, Open5GS's SMF versus ours (request sequence, information elements per message)
rows.evidence: Identical request sequence (establishment, modification, deletion); every element Open5GS's SMF sends is either sent by ours or on the documented allow-list (charging URR, user id, match-all filters, IPv6 router-solicitation forwarding).

rows.procedure: UE IPv4 address and IPv6 /64 prefix pools per DNN: allocation, rotation, exhaustion, release on every path
rows.evidence: Pool exhaustion rejects with cause #26; addresses are returned on release, replacement, refusal and AMF failure.

rows.procedure: Nudm_SDM session management subscription data per slice and DNN; Nudm_UECM SMF registration and deregistration
rows.evidence: Against our UDM (and, in S3, through it from Open5GS's AMF).

rows.procedure: Npcf_SMPolicyControl create / delete; the decision (session AMBR, default QoS, PCC rules, QoS data) drives NAS, N2 and N4
rows.evidence: Against our PCF with a GBR voice rule; S3 against the same PCF with Open5GS's AMF and UERANSIM.

rows.procedure: Configuration: strict keys, address formats, ranges; nothing is bound by --check
rows.evidence: About 50 SMF-specific negative cases plus the sample and compose configurations.

rows.procedure: Hostile peer input (multipart, NAS, N2, IPFilterRule, policy JSON, bit rates, PFCP responses) is bounded and never crashes
rows.evidence: Replay fuzzing with deterministic mutations under ASan/UBSan; ThreadSanitizer run of the end-to-end test.

rows.procedure: PCF-initiated SM policy update: the decision is diffed against the one in force (session AMBR, flow rates, rules and flows added / removed), the UPF is modified (Update QER, Create / Remove PDR and QER) before anyone is told
rows.evidence: Scenario S4 with OUR_SMF=1: the PCF pushes a throttled AMBR and a new rule to our SMF, the UPF is modified, the AMF sends the gNB a PDUSessionResourceModifyRequest and the session keeps carrying traffic. The unit test checks the QFI of downlink traffic before and after against the real UPF engine.

rows.procedure: PDU SESSION MODIFICATION COMMAND towards the UE (new Session-AMBR, QoS rules created / deleted, QoS flow descriptions created / modified / deleted), PTI 0; the UE's complete is accepted
rows.evidence: Decoded again with the NAS library; Open5GS's AMF forwards it to the gNB. UERANSIM's UE has no handling for the message, so the UE side is not exercised.

rows.procedure: PDUSessionResourceModifyRequestTransfer: new session AMBR, QoS flows added / modified, flows to release
rows.evidence: Encoded with the generated APER schema and decoded again; reaches the gNB through Open5GS's AMF (S4).

rows.procedure: PCF-initiated termination of the SM policy association releases the PDU session through the AMF and the UE, guarded by a timer
rows.evidence: Release command with PTI 0 delivered; the release complete frees everything; without it the guard timer does.

rows.procedure: A UPF that restarts (changed Recovery Time Stamp) or stays unreachable is handled: its sessions are released towards the UE / AMF (release command, status notification), the PCF, UDM and the address pool are cleaned
rows.evidence: The UPF process is stopped and restarted on the same ports; no stale session is left in the SMF, the UPF, the PCF or the pools.

rows.procedure: Network-triggered service request: a Downlink Data Report for an idle session becomes an N1N2MessageTransfer with the N2 setup request and no N1 message
rows.evidence: The AMF receives the transfer after the downlink packet is buffered; the report is acknowledged first.

rows.procedure: SM contexts survive an SMF restart: state file written atomically after every change, addresses and policy restored, the SMF's own Recovery Time Stamp kept (a changed stamp would make the UPFs drop its sessions), sessions of a UPF that restarted meanwhile released
rows.evidence: Restart with the UPF alive: the restored context deactivates and releases normally. Restart with the UPF restarted in between: the sessions are released towards the AMF.

rows.procedure: The AMF is discovered through the NRF by the servingNfId the AMF sent (Nnrf_NFDiscovery, cached for a minute); an unknown AMF falls back to the host of the smContextStatusUri
rows.evidence: Scripted NRF; against the Open5GS NRF in S3/S4 the SMF registers with smfInfo and the Open5GS AMF finds it.

rows.procedure: IPv6 router advertisement: the UE's router solicitation is forwarded by the UPF to the SMF (control-plane PDR and FAR with GTP-U to the SMF), the advertisement with the session's /64 and the MTU goes back through the UPF
rows.evidence: Checksum, hop limit and type validated as RFC 4861 asks; end to end through the real UPF runtime to the gNB tunnel.

rows.procedure: Hostile policy pairs and solicitations (identifier assignment, modification builders, router advertisement) never crash
rows.evidence: Replay fuzzing with mutations under ASan/UBSan.

rows.procedure: UE-requested PDU session modification (requested QoS rules / flows, packet filter operations)
rows.evidence: A UE modification request is answered with a PDU SESSION MODIFICATION REJECT (cause #31). Network-initiated modification is complete; mapping the UE's request to a PCF update (UE-initiated resource modification) is not.

rows.procedure: Charging (CHF / usage reporting URRs), ATSSS, Ethernet and unstructured PDU session types, SSC modes 2 and 3, handover procedures, I-SMF / V-SMF roles, discovery of UPFs through the NRF
rows.evidence: UPFs are configured peers; only SSC mode 1 and IP session types are offered; usage reports from the UPF are not requested.
